question: Can Signal Temporal Logic specifications be interpreted as poset stratifications of decision space-time, and does an STL-robustness-trained RL agent encode corresponding singular strata in its latent representation?

key_findings.claim: Policies and target histories can be encoded as order-preserving maps into posets, giving a broad stratification semantics for discrete decision problems.
key_findings.evidence: A no-rotation Minigrid policy induces a map from a digitized cell complex into its policy tree, while a continuous trajectory maps to the closed set of times at which it intersects a target, ordered by reverse inclusion.

key_findings.claim: The derivative of multiscale neighborhood-volume growth distinguishes some strata that one-number local-dimension estimators miss.
key_findings.evidence: On rendered room-corridor and hourglass examples, local dimension drops or changes slope across scale. VGT-dot clustering retains a signature at the hourglass neck that Dimension Induced Clustering misses, while HADES localizes singularities more precisely but at higher computational cost.

key_findings.claim: The paper connects STL atomic predicates to tubular neighborhoods of semi-algebraic strata and uses formula robustness as a delayed RL reward.
key_findings.evidence: Distance-to-stratum predicates are proposed from maximal tubular neighborhoods. Two MemoryGym tasks reward normalized robustness of 'eventually in green' and 'eventually in green and always not in red' only after a 195-step trajectory; PPO trains a Transformer-XL policy over current and ten recent frames.

anchors.section: III-C STL Formulation and IV-A STL-Reward Based Game

key_findings.claim: The first task's latent-token cloud contains a visually apparent hourglass-like transition aligned with the externally visible STL timing cue.
key_findings.evidence: Across 250 trajectories and 48,500 256D token embeddings, rendered UMAP plots separate frames with an empty versus filled green square. VGT-dot clusters vary around the connecting neck, and HADES rejections after 100D projection concentrate near that neck and some late-trajectory boundary points.

anchors.section: IV-B.1 Eventually in the green square

key_findings.claim: Evidence for stratification in the more complex avoid-red task is weaker and remains qualitative.
key_findings.evidence: The second task has about 12,000 unique vectors; HADES exceeds available memory even after reduction to 100D. UMAP and ISOMAP plus two VGT-dot clusters show a similar two-lobe/core-boundary pattern, which the authors explicitly label weaker evidence.

IV-B.2 Eventually in green and always not in red

method.core_idea: Use poset-valued stratification maps to represent policy, state, and target-history structure; translate STL predicates into neighborhoods of strata; then test whether an STL-reward-trained agent's embeddings show corresponding multiscale singular geometry.
method.mechanism: The theory digitizes state spaces or orders space-time by reachability, records target intersections with face/overlap/order posets, and defines STL predicates through distance-based rug functions. Numerically, local neighborhood volume is measured over radii, smoothed, differentiated, and clustered as VGT-dot; UMAP/ISOMAP visualize the cloud and HADES supplies a local manifold-null test where memory permits.
assumptions: Relevant state and target sets admit useful poset or compact semi-algebraic stratifications.
The topology imposed on a digitized MDP and continuity required of a policy capture the operational decision problem.
Local sample density and multiscale volume growth in learned embeddings reflect intrinsic strata rather than visitation frequency or projection artifacts.
The visible square that marks when an STL operator is active is an acceptable cue for studying temporally induced latent structure.
A terminal robustness score after the full trajectory provides adequate learning signal for the two demonstration tasks.

techniques.role: Encodes adjacency, reachability, target overlap, or trajectory history as an order-preserving map.
Turns temporal-logic satisfaction margin into a scalar terminal reward for PPO.
Measures how neighborhood mass changes with radius to expose local dimension and transitions between strata.
Clusters complete VGT derivative curves so local-to-global geometry is not collapsed to one dimension estimate.
Uses HADES as an independent local manifold-null check at candidate pinch points.

evaluations.setting: Synthetic room-corridor and hourglass point clouds
evaluations.metric: Qualitative agreement of local-dimension estimators, HADES, DIC, and VGT-dot with known boundaries and singularities
evaluations.result: HADES localizes boundaries and singular points; VGT-dot retains a neck signature missed by DIC and exposes scale-dependent slope changes
evaluations.baseline: Three local intrinsic-dimension estimators, Dimension Induced Clustering, and HADES

evaluations.setting: 250 length-194 trajectories in the 'eventually green' MemoryGym task, 48,500 total 256D tokens and about 7,600 unique vectors
evaluations.metric: UMAP geometry, VGT-dot agglomerative clusters, and HADES manifold-null rejections after 100D projection
evaluations.result: Two lobes track empty versus filled square observations; VGT-dot changes around the neck and HADES rejections concentrate near the neck plus part of the late-trajectory boundary
evaluations.baseline: Agreement across VGT-dot, HADES, and time/cue coloring; no agent, reward, or random-network ablation

evaluations.setting: The 'eventually green and always not red' task with about 12,000 unique 256D token vectors
evaluations.metric: UMAP/ISOMAP structure and two-cluster VGT-dot coloring
evaluations.result: A two-lobe, symmetric core-to-boundary pattern is visible, but HADES cannot run within available memory

limitations: The authors describe all neural results as preliminary and call for more robust tubular-neighborhood volume laws and automated stratum extraction.
The authors explicitly weaken the second-task claim because HADES exceeds memory even after projection to 100 dimensions.
No policy return, STL satisfaction rate, training curve, seed variability, or comparison against a non-STL reward is reported.
The dominant two-lobe separation follows a directly visible empty/filled square cue, so it does not isolate geometry caused by the robustness reward or temporal reasoning.
Reviewer inference: UMAP, ISOMAP, density variation, duplicate removal, and projection can each create or amplify apparent necks; no null embedding or label-permutation test is shown.
Reviewer inference: Definition III.3's 'away from S' predicate d(S,x)>=0 is tautologically true for ordinary distance, suggesting either a typo or an unusable predicate as written.

Reviewer inference: a maximal neighborhood membership test identifies a tube around a stratum, not exact stratum membership, so the claimed STL correspondence needs a sharper semantics and proof for Boolean and temporal compositions.
failure_modes: State-visitation density can mimic a local dimension change even when the support is one smooth manifold.
A low-dimensional projection can fold separated regions together or manufacture a pinch point that is absent in 256 dimensions.
Terminal STL robustness creates a non-Markovian, delayed reward whose required history scales poorly for nested or long-horizon formulas.
A visible operator-status cue can let the policy cluster observations without internally representing the temporal specification.
VGT-dot clustering requires a chosen radius range, smoothing rule, cluster count, and metric; different choices can change inferred strata.
General MDPs with rotations, stochastic transitions, multiple goals, or discontinuous policies may not admit the paper's simple tree-stratified construction.
reusable_insights: Analyze an RL environment's ambient state and trajectory stratification before assigning semantic meaning to clusters in its learned latent space.
Keep the full neighborhood-growth curve when geometry changes across scale; one intrinsic-dimension estimate can miss singular junctions.
Use a statistically calibrated singularity test as a check on visualization and clustering, and record when it fails computationally.
A temporal-logic reward experiment needs cue, reward, policy, projection, and visitation ablations to distinguish learned temporal structure from observation structure.
Automata or explicit memory state should be compared with terminal robustness when evaluating long-horizon STL learning signal.
open_questions: Does the latent stratification persist when the operator-active square is removed and time must be inferred from history?
Are VGT-dot strata stable across network seeds, checkpoints, held-out trajectories, density equalization, and projection methods?
Can strata be recovered in the original embedding space with calibrated false-discovery control and tractable memory?
How should the STL-to-strata semantics handle complements, overlapping tubes, nested temporal operators, and the tautological away predicate as written?
Does matching an ambient poset predict better policy generalization, safety, or failure localization?
Can reward-machine state make the STL reward Markovian while preserving the proposed geometric correspondence?

competitive_landscape.title: Reward Machines for Signal Temporal Logic
competitive_landscape.difference: Reward Machines compiles STL into timed alternating automata with clock state and Markovian rewards, directly addressing the history and long-horizon weakness of terminal robustness. Stratifying RL instead uses robustness as given and studies the geometry it may induce, without improving reward tractability.

competitive_landscape.title: Tractable Reinforcement Learning of Signal Temporal Logic Objectives
competitive_landscape.difference: Venkataraman et al. compress the state history needed for STL satisfaction, optimize an approximation to satisfaction probability, and give a performance bound. This paper instead uses full-trajectory delayed robustness and contributes a topological interpretation and latent diagnostic rather than a tractable control algorithm.

competitive_landscape.title: Temporal Logic Specification-Conditioned Decision Transformer for Offline Safe Reinforcement Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: Specification-conditioned Decision Transformers condition offline policies on STL rules and evaluate safety and reward on DSRL benchmarks. Stratifying RL trains online with one fixed robustness reward and inspects one internal layer, offering geometric semantics but far less policy-level evaluation.

competitive_landscape.title: Token Embeddings Violate the Manifold Hypothesis
competitive_landscape.difference: Robinson et al. formulate a statistically testable fiber-bundle null and connect rejected token neighborhoods to output instability across several language models. Stratifying RL extends the non-manifold viewpoint to policy embeddings and relates it to ambient task structure, but its evidence is mainly visual and task-specific.

competitive_landscape.title: HADES: Fast Singularity Detection with Local Measure Comparison
competitive_landscape.difference: HADES provides a kernel goodness-of-fit singularity test with recovery theory for transverse manifold intersections and diverse empirical validation. VGT-dot is cheaper and preserves a multiscale signature, but currently lacks comparable statistical guarantees and is benchmarked against HADES only on small or projected samples.
competitive_landscape.source_version: arXiv v1, 2023-11-07; later SIAM J. Mathematics of Data Science 2025

novelty_assessment: The authors claim a novel correspondence between STL and poset stratification, plus a scalable VGT-derivative signature for STL-trained RL embeddings. Reviewer inference: connecting ambient task posets, temporal predicates, and latent singularities is genuinely unusual and generative of testable ideas. However, existing STL-RL methods already use robustness rewards, and existing geometry work already rejects manifold structure; the new causal bridge between those two facts is not yet established by the cue-heavy, unablated demonstrations.
reviewer_notes: Read all eight pages and inspected the rendered latent plots in Figures 11–13. The plots support only qualitative structural claims: the square-status cue visibly explains much of the split, and HADES is unavailable for the harder task. The distance predicate and theorem wording were checked directly against page 6. Competitor records and current arXiv/PMLR versions were verified on 2026-08-23.
